At least Gifted. A master manipulator who can weaponize her situation to sway even those with good heads and kind hearts to her side. Her persuasion abilities rival that of The Joker and she has been able to pull off feats such as taking over an entire prison, causing a large amount of teenagers to support her, and convince the public that she was innocent. In terms of combat, she's shown to be reasonably skilled in fighting, able to go toe-to-toe with Nightwing, Harley Quinn, Batgirl, and even Batman, using her wits to stay one step ahead of her opponents.
Overconfident in her abilities often has her fight foes much stronger than her. Furthermore

His fight with Rogol is said to cause the Phantom Zone to tremble from this fight, and Superman has said he could destroy said realm if he puts his mind to it. Broke a hole in the source wall, which is several layers above the Godsphere. Destroyed the World Forger's Multiverse, likely consisting of up to the 5th dimension, considering a corrupted Myxy and how he's a sixth dimensional entity, with one punch. The 5th Dimension itself is an infinite layer above the Godsphere, and the 6th dimension is an infinite layer above that. This was during a dip in 6th dimensional suns however, so it's unknown whether he can access this normally. Knocked out Auter.io and Barbatos with one punch, both of which being able to create and destroy stories. These would be inconsistent with his encounter with Mandrakk however, who could cause similar damage, yet Superman needed the Cosmic Armor to match. States that his mind and body are stronger than they've ever been, potentially including his amp from the 6th dimension, however it's unknown whether or not this is accurate, as the other statements he brings up in this moment are already comparable to his older self. Most of these feats affect areas far, far above the infinite dimenisons in DC.)

Extraversal (Survived being within the Void from Lois Lane's call for help. Could survive various forces of the Cosmology, such as speed and gods, and repel it with his heat vision. Endured the destruction of the Source Wall)

Immeasurable (Shattered Space, Time and the bounds of Infinity, escaping to another Universe, just trying to find Supergirl. Flew to a dead Universe. For reference, a DC Universe is infinite in size, so he likely broke the bounds of it again to get here. Can travel through time by moving fast enough. Escaped the Source, despite it having no direction or end. Perceived drifting through no time, or perhaps all of time, one point in time where it merged into said point. It's possible this doesn't scale to his flight speed and possibly just reactions though, assuming it isn't hyperbole. Potentially escaped a prison of Hypertime, which seems to be above Limbo. We only see his cape however, so it's a bit vague to consider. Said himself that he can cross distances that cease to be distance.) Irrelevant

Holds back very often in fights, at least during Post-Crisis and Post-Flashpoint, has shown to struggle with several feats around Planetary or Solar System Level, this is largely due to him unintentionally holding back, rather than actively showing his true strength. NOTE 2: While the three different eras of Superman are shown to have variable stats and abilities, they have also shown to fight on par with each other and comparable entities, meaning at least physically, they should scale to one another, hence why only Rebirth Superman is considered to determine their primary stats.

This was during a dip in 6th dimensional suns however, so it's unknown whether he can access this normally. Knocked out Auter.io and Barbatos with one punch, both of which being able to create and destroy stories. These would be inconsistent with his encounter with Mandrakk however, who could cause similar damage, yet Superman needed the Cosmic Armor to match. States that his mind and body are stronger than they've ever been, potentially including his amp from the 6th dimension, however it's unknown whether or not this is accurate, as the other statements he brings up in this moment are already comparable to his older self. Most of these feats affect areas far, far above the infinite dimenisons in DC.)

Extraversal (Survived being within the Void from Lois Lane's call for help. Could survive various forces of the Cosmology, such as speed and gods, and repel it with his heat vision. Endured the destruction of the Source Wall)

Escaped the Source, despite it having no direction or end. Perceived drifting through no time, or perhaps all of time, one point in time where it merged into said point. It's possible this doesn't scale to his flight speed and possibly just reactions though, assuming it isn't hyperbole. Potentially escaped a prison of Hypertime, which seems to be above Limbo. We only see his cape however, so it's a bit vague to consider. Said himself that he can cross distances that cease to be distance.) Irrelevant

Darkseid is vulnerable to Radion, which is a lethal substance to New Gods., Omega Effect: Uxas was reborn as Darkseid when he absorbed the full power of the Omega Effect from the Infinity Pit. Thanks to the Omega energies he gained incredible power and a wide array of abilities., Omega Beams: Darkseid's signature technique involves firing a thin, red energy beam from each eye. These beams, also known as "Finder Beams", are extremely fast and home in on their target, passing through physical barriers if needed. Once contact is made, they can either erase the target from existence, or transport them through time and space according to Darkseid's will. He can also use them to recreate dead beings, or paralyze his target while probing their weakness., Omega Sanction: Also known as the Life Trap, the Omega Sanction can take two completely different forms depending on Darkseid's intent. The first simply sends his target back in time, forcing them to live out their life in the past. The second, stated by Grant Morrison to happen when Darkseid decides on being crueler than normal, was only displayed by Godhead Darkseid. It traps the victim in a never-ending series of horrible realities that force them to live out worse and worse lives, until their soul breaks., Energy Absorption: Darkseid is an immensely powerful energy absorber, capable of completely draining the energies of powerful beings like Mordru and all of Sorcerers' World to help restore his own power. His absorption is so powerful that he ordered his servants to get away from him lest they be killed, and some of his servants were capable of taking on Pre-Crisis Kryptonians and Daxamites., Energy Shockwaves: Darkseid can create shockwaves of energy by raising his hands., Spacetime Warping: Darkseid can generate a gravitational pull so intense that space twists and time is pulled, so that those inside live days between seconds., Boom Tubes: Darkseid can summon boom tubes at will, as well as control the paths of others' boom tubes. These portals can transport their user throughout space and between dimensions. They automatically adjust the size of their user to be suitable for their destination, which is why Darkseid appears human-sized rather than star-sized when travelling to the mortal universe., Telepathy: Darkseid has incredibly powerful telepathic abilities. He can forcefully drain information out of his target's mind as well as control others with his will. While in a weakened state during the Great Darkness Saga, he controlled three billion Daxamites at once. He was able to force his mind into others' from across dimensional gaps., Avatars: Darkseid can create duplicate bodies from portions of his energy that can function autonomously. They are significantly weaker than his real body but otherwise seem to retain his intellect and abilities. As all instances of Darkseid seen in lower-dimensional realms are infinitesimally small parts of Darkseid's true being, it stands to reason that Godhead Darkseid possesses all of the abilities demonstrated by them but to a much greater degree. Furthermore, he also possessed the Anti-Life Equation, using it to dominate much of Earth's populace in the moments before everything would be destroyed., Omega Beams: A single use of the Omega Beams, used when Darkseid was dying and possessing the body of a cancer-ridden Dan Turpin, contained enough energy to destroy time itself., Omega Sanction: The version of the Sanction used by the True Darkseid is infinitely more powerful and cruel than the Sanction demonstrated by his Pre-Flashpoint emanation. Rather than displacing its target through time it traps them in a never-ending succession of dark realities that inflict endless suffering upon the prisoner., Possession: Darkseid can incarnate in the lower-dimensional mortal universe by possessing the body of a mortal. However, to truly incarnate he needs to corrupt the body of a good soul, which was why his first attempt at incarnating via a mob boss was a failure., Anti-Life Equation: Using the Anti-Life Equation, Darkseid was able to assume total control over everyone who had been exposed to the broadcasted equation, effectively gaining three billion new bodies at once. The victims were completely subsumed by Darkseid's will, speaking with his voice and moving according to his desire.

Universe level+ (Fought Golden Age Superman in Infinite Crisis to a stalemate, where both altered timelines and shattered the boundaries of space and time, and furthermore were outright stated to be going for the destruction of eachother's universes. Both would later shatter the universe again, and the DC Comics site backs up the DCU shaking apart. Comparable to Shazam, who fought the Invincible Man, who siphoned power from the soul of the Universe, created by the Big Bang. Fought Black Adam, who Superman said hits harder than Shazam/Captain Marvel, and who survived a tesseract expanding in his head, Shazam himself could also survive a tesseract bomb. Knocked down Superboy-Prime, who was planning to destroy the universe by flying into Oa, causing a new big bang and leaving himself only. Tussled with Nebula Man, literally a living Universe. Fought with 30th Century Mordru, who wields all the magical power of Universe-247. Fought Monarch, who stated his Quantum power was akin to the Big Bang, and whose fight with Captain Atom was twisting space and time and causing compressed universes to explode. Fought many Imperiex Probes for several days, where one could fight and mortally wound Aquaman, who was causing the universe to collapse in on itself. Very capable of fighting Kyle Rayner, and walking through a full-power blast from him, the same Kyle that took down an Abberation that was breaking down the laws of reality, and was stated to threaten the universe, and was able to revert these changes by amplifying his ring. Took down Starman, who overwhelmed Darklord Maaldor, the latter of whom possessed an entire universe. Decked Blackstar, who can manipulate the energies of the cosmos as he wills) | At least Universe level+, likely far higher (Unfathomably stronger than his base, to a practically indescribable extent. Through Superman's history, he has had an ingrained mental block preventing the use of his full strength, due to his usual refusal to kill or cause severe harm. This is even present when he looks to be enraged. It's only after training with Mongul that Superman first uses his full power. On the two occasions that Superman went all out: Superman thoroughly and utterly stomped Doomsday in their rematch, to the point where Doomday's claws shattered like glass on Superman's chest. After having his soul split in two by the Phantom Stranger, in order to take on Hell, heavily weakening and corrupting him, but removing his restraints, he effortlessly one-shot all of his previous villains including powerhouses like Darkseid and Doomsday; also instantly killing Brainiac by just shuffling his hands, and Lex in his war suit by spitting at him.) | At least Universe level+ (Much stronger than his base form. When Mxyzptlk created a Doomsday clone amped by 5th Dimensional magic, Superman was gradually overpowering it, only being unable to win due to Mxy recreating plot elements from The Death of Superman. After being easily digitized by Brainiac 13 in base, reformed as Superman Blue, then fought against him, with Brainiac 13 stated as a ravager of timelines. Can fight the Lord of Time, who is four-dimensional) | Outerverse level via Hax (In the mental arena of the Theta State, was able to fight and defeat Dominus, sealing him in a Phantom Zone that Dominus created. The Phantom Zone is described as boundless, and a dimensionless dimension, placed in the Sphere of the Gods, thereby placing it in the same figure of speech as even the weakest New Gods, existing beyond DC's outerversal timestream, and are described as existing in a platonic, archetypal world) | High Outerverse level (Is as large as an outerversal New God, where the Sphere of the Gods transcends other outerversal realms itself. Fought and managed to defeat Sivaa, who is capable of obliterating creation by just dancing. Fought off Scott Free, who was using the full Anti-Life Equation, the parallel of the Source. Scales to Darkseid's true form, having fought him numerous times, and a last-ditch effort managed to break Soulfire Darkseid in half, who was millions of times stronger than his base, of which is relied on by the Source to exist along with Highfather. The latter was likely due to Superman briefly not holding back.) | Up to Extraverse level (The Story/Flaw itself is far above even Monitor - Mind the Overvoid, who was forced to scab over it with Divine Metals, making the Thought Robot, unable to defend against it otherwise. Even sealed, The Thought Robot, powered by the Story, managed to defeat Mandrakk the Dark Monitor. Allowed Superman himself to survive being in the Overvoid, and allowed him to fly back to Lois Lane in creation, shattering Neron's infinite layers of Hell. After being pushed constantly by his own Death, Superman rose above creation, transcending it so much to see it as a dream, and then one-shot his own Death upon his return. Scales to all other feats performed with the Story's power from previous and future Supermen)

Immesurable in Combat and normally (Casually backhanded Zoom, who said Superman had speed rivalling his own. Zoom himself can run to the 25th Century, and can freely move through time. Reacted to Wally West and Barry Allen running through the timestream, both of whom accidentally ran a few weeks into the future, and Superman casually kept pace with both Wally and Jay Garrick. Even held back as usual, he tied in a race with Barry Allen. Chased Superboy into the future. Literally outran time stop. Should scale to Superboy-Prime, who briefly outpaced Jeni Ognat when she ran through time. Should scale to Hal Jordan, who managed to penetrate time. Is the equal of an elder Golden Age Superman, who broke the time barrier, ran back three centuries, and casually flew back to his own time), Irrelevant maximum Flight Speed (Flew through the Bleed with Overman and Shazam in order to stop Mandrakk's reality blitzing missiles. Flew back from Apokolips to Earth, which is situated beyond the Bleed in the Sphere of the Gods. Flew out of the Source Wall, despite Highfather saying it was impossible. Comparable to Wonder Woman, who flew into the Speed Force itself. Possibly compares to Silver Age Superman, who a younger Golden Age Superman fought, who flew so fast that the Spectre had to stop him from flying into realms that "no mortal eye may be permitted to behold") | Immesurable in Combat and normally, Irrelevant maximum Flight Speed | Irrelevant (Stated he could reach the Source Wall instantly, with Metron choosing Superman Blue over Light Ray, implying that Superman Blue is superior in speed to him) | Irrelevant via Hax (Kept up with and tagged Dominus) | Irrelevant (Can keep up with true form Darkseid along with other powerful New Gods) | Up to Irrelevant (Allowed Superman to easily fly back to Earth after being left in the Overvoid, and after rising above creation against his own Death)

Universe level+ (Can take attacks from those he can harm. Withstood Aztek unleashing all of his 4-dimensional energy in self-destruction. Took an extremely heavy punch from Icon, who killed Starbreaker, who themself can kill someone who was holding the universe together.), Regeneration and Immutability makes him difficult to kill. | At least Universe level+, likely far higher, Regeneration and Immutability makes him difficult to kill. | At least Universe level+, Incorporeality and Regeneration makes him very difficult to kill. | Outerverse level via Hax | High Outerverse level | Up to Extraverse level, Plot and Fate Manipulation make him almost impossible to kill, even by beings potent in said powers themselves.

Standard Kryptonian weaknesses, but has survived situations that would kill an average Kryptonian, including tanking anti-sunlight on the way to disabling Mageddon, fighting a Kryptonite clone of Doomsday, and once continued to fight even after having the iron in his blood turned to Kryptonite. Magic is said to be a weakness of his, but it just bypasses his immutability, having resisted powerful magic on many occassions. Refuses to kill on most occassions, and mentally blocks himself from using more of his power, As before, but no longer holds back his full power, Being forced to transform back into normal leaves him powerless., possibly characters with stronger Chi Manipulation, as usual Mind Manipulation does not work on the Theta State, Normal base weaknesses, Nothing Notable Note 1: If you are confused about certain cosmological structures in DC Comics, please refer to this explainer by WebCamParrot. I will also, at some point, be creating a DC Cosmology page for those who prefer a text/diagram form. Note 2: It is unreasonable to handwave away the rather abundant amount of Universal+ AP and Immesurable speed scaling in DC Comics. This is for two reasons:, First off, Superman holds back through all of his appearances, save at least two. This means that he would be holding back in any of the few low-end outliers, but equally that he would be holding back in virtually all of the sheer abundance of Universal+ AP/Immesurable Speed feats he performs. To further this, we see what happens in Superman 666 when Superman doesn't hold back, even severely weakened, he shows he can effortlessly blitz and one-shot all the villains usually considered a threat to him, which is testament to the levels that Superman can restrain himself to., there are zero rules for how powerful you can make a character. It is utterly fallacious to say "Superman makes more sense being solar system level because he absorbs power from a star" or "It would be weird for him to be faster than time itself, so he isn't", when dozens upon dozens of instances say he can threaten the universe, and move fast enough to travel through time. You cannot just use the incredibly arbitrary and nonsensical "what makes sense" in powerscaling, because fiction doesn't obey real life

This Darkseid was also stated to regularly consume and destroy universes. Fodderized Alan Scott, despite him being empowered by the all of the Green throughout the multiverse. Far stronger than the vast majority of the New and Old Gods. Is a threat to the Source itself. Stomped Eclipso, forcing him to serve Darkseid. Similarly, Darkseid stated that the Spectre had no power on Apokolips. Created Stayne, a rival in power to Takion, who embodies the Source. Fought evenly with a weakened Anti-Monitor, only losing due the Anti-Monitor using the God of Death Flash. Cracked the Source Wall in his fight with Highfather. Scales to Sivaa through boomtube Superman, who was going to destroy all of creation by dancing. Immesurable (Has blitzed numerous characters on this level), possibly Irrelevant travel speed (via scaling to Superman and the Flash) | Irrelevant (Via sheer size. Universe level+ (Could survive attacks from an Alan Scott empowered by the Green, the Gray, the Blue, the Red and the White.) | High Outerverse level (A blaster than could kill anyone on Apokolips, excluding Kalibak, would effectively be useless on Darkseid. Vulnerable to Radion, a substance that the New Gods are weak to. Furthermore, he was also weakened prior to being shot by the radion bullet, that would kill him in Final Crisis. To use possession, 000 = 1, 000x increase in power. ## Exponential - 10x multiplier stacks exponentially... which results in a 10100, 000x power multiplier. that is a ten followed by a hundred-thousand zeroes. Which, is utterly absurd (if a million wasn't crazy already). #DARKSEID DOES NOT USE AVATARS ALL THE TIME - This is a major misconception about Darkseid, where it's claimed his "true form" is the Essence form we see in Final Crisis, and he just uses emanations outside of this. It isn't. Darkseid actually dislikes using avatars, stated. To visit the regular universe, Darkseid uses boomtubes to massively reduce his own size. Aside from when DeSaad was impersonating the New God, Darkseid is mostly always in his "true form" even if he has to shrink down to visit the universe. ##This is the same logic by which Superman becomes able to stand

Varies from 5-A to High 4-C at his peak

His powers and abilities don't vary in the same way his statistics do, and as such they can be listed all together. *Superhuman Physical Characteristics (See Attack Potency, Speed, Lifting Strength, and Durability) *Combat Expertise (Was an experienced gladiator, managing to contend skill-wise with Superman and Draaga) * Stealth Mastery (Snuck up on Wonder Woman, defeating her "before she knew (he) was there") *Preparation (Seems to have sought out the Black Mercy to incapacitate Superman, allowing for an easier victory) With Preparation, he can utilize: *Energy Projection (with his Planet-Busting Energy Cannon) *Illusion Creation (The Black Mercy latches onto its target, trapping them in an illusion of their greatest desire)

Varies (Mongul's power level is overtly somewhat inconsistent. In "War World," he is overtly relative to (if not slightly weaker than) JL Season 1 Superman - whereas during "For the Man who has Everything," which is during JLU, he is capable of holding his own against a furious Superman. This is plainly inconsistent, considering JL Season 1 Superman is far weaker than his other DCAU appearances, even in the words of Bruce Timm himself), from Brown Dwarf Level (Scaling to 1.002 Quettatons - Was overtly equal to Draaga (only losing their fistfight presumably because he was already exhausted from fighting Superman), who fought JL Season 1 Superman and could even inflict small flesh wounds on him with strikes - with Mongul similarly fighting Superman and having a temporary upper hand, albeit Superman was unable to truly fight back because he believed Mongul would destroy Draaga's planet if he did. Despite being weaker than he is during STAS, JL Season 2, and JLU, JL Season 1 Superman is still powerful enough to overpower the beam of a Manhunter, which can beam struggle with a serious Green Lantern), up to Large Star Level at his peak (Scaling to 1.664 Foe - Fought a furious, standard-strength Superman during "For the Man who has Everything," and despite being overtly somewhat weaker (at one point, he himself admitted a volley of punches from Superman could have killed him had Superman not regained his wits), he was able to hurt him and temporarily gain the upper hand at a few points during their fight despite Superman being so furious during this battle that it's strongly implied he would have broken his no-kill code had he not stopped himself - Batman even believed Mongul could kill Superman if Superman was left defenseless by the Black Mercy. Soundly overpowered a furious Wonder Woman, viewing her as little more than an annoyance (despite Diana being able to budge his head with blows - however, said blows did no actual damage and, in reality, only hurt Wonder Woman's hands) - with producer Dwayne McDuffie referring to this fight as Wonder Woman getting an "ass-whupping" and Batman being sure Mongul could kill her)

Varies, from Relativistic+ (Scaling to 0.53c - Scales (via Draaga) in speed to JL Season 1 Superman, who despite having his powers lessened could keep up with a battle-ready Wonder Woman) to FTL (Scaling to 2.3c - Kept up with an enraged standard-strength Superman, landing attacks on him, and landed attacks on an alert Wonder Woman)

Varies, from Brown Dwarf Level (Scaling to 1.002 Quettatons - Should scale to his own durability as per Newton's Third Law, and could keep fighting after several blows from a bloodlusted Draaga - Draaga being capable of giving JL Season 1 Superman small flesh wounds with his attacks), up to up to Large Star Level at his peak (Scaling to 1.664 Foe - Got up and performed a knee strike after several blows to the face from a furious Superman (with Superman being so enraged at the time that it's all but stated that he nearly broke his no-kill code against Mongul), even staying in the fight, albeit with injury, after taking a blast of Heat Vision to the chest. Was so durable that an enraged Wonder Woman striking him twice in the face hurt her hands more than it hurt Mongul himself, with the furious strikes doing little more than budging Mongul's head, with none of WW's other attacks doing anything more than annoying him)

Is extremely cocky and prideful. Note: Mongul appears in the novel "Wild at Heart," which at the time was meant to be a tie-in to the DCAU continuity. However, the fact that Hawkgirl very clearly meets Lobo for the first time during JL Season 2's "Hereafter" does not mesh with the fact that she clearly does not know him and is meeting him for the first time during the novel - there's no way Hawkgirl could have met Lobo for the first time twice. Since the onscreen episode naturally takes precedent, it logically follows that the novel is not canon and his feats within said novel can be disregarded. Category:Goulden1998 Category:Tier 5

Cannot survive more than an hour without his suit and helmet. His glass helmet is his weak spot. His body must remain in cold temperatures or he will die if removed from his suit. Notable Attacks/Techniques: *Freeze Shattering- Mr. Freeze uses his ice based weaponry to freeze a foe into a solid block of ice. He than breaks the ice block, causing the foe's body to shatter. This can be used as a form of Durability Negation, provided his freezing abilities would even work on the foe. If the ice block is not shattered, the person will remain trapped until they either thaw out or freeze to death. Even normal humans can last a while, though they will die after some time. At least 9-A physically, higher with his Cold Gun, from 8-B to 7-C to 7-A with Preparation | At least 9-A physically, at least High 8-C+ with his Cold Gun, and 7-C to 7-A with Preparation | At least 9-A physically, higher with his Cold Arm Cannons

In his first two keys, Freeze boasts: * Superhuman Physical Characteristics (See Attack Potency, Speed, Lifting Strength, and Durability) * Genius Intelligence (See Intelligence) * Weapon Mastery (with his Cold Gun and his future suit's cold arm cannons) * Preparation (Prepared a reverse-fusion bomb in "Deep Freeze" and a massive cold gun in "Heart of Ice") * Longevity (Freeze's aging has almost completely halted, and after decades hasn't aged a day, as seen in Batman Beyond's "Meltdown") * Self-Sustenance (Type 2, and seemingly Type 3) * Energy Projection, Ice Manipulation, and Light Manipulation (The blasts from his laser-powered Cold Gun (and the blasts from his future suit's arm cannons) freeze essentially anything they touch in a matter of moments - technically, this is moreso a direct effect of the gun's blasts utilizing Temperature Manipulation) * Paralysis Inducement via Freezing (Freezing his foes holds them in place, incapacitating them without necessarily harming them) * Resistance to Extreme Cold/Ice Manipulation (Due to his chemically-altered body, not only is Freeze immune to the adverse effects of extreme cold, he thrives in extremely cold temperatures) With Optional Equipment, he can utilize: * Flight (with a Helicopter) * Natural Weaponry (Conventional: His Polar Bears have fangs and claws) In his Batman Beyond appearance, he retains his prior abilities, possibly sans Immortality and Self-Sustenance due to his transplant into another body.

At least Small Building Level physically (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - Overtly stronger than Batman, easily tossing him and restraining him with one arm. Effortlessly kicked locked doors off their hinges. Grant Walker, while wearing a replica of Freeze's suit, bent a metal operating table with a punch), at least Small Building Level+, likely higher with his Cold Gun (0.245 Tons - Froze a garage door, and its freezing power is likely greater in magnitude considering how quickly it caused this level of ice buildup and froze a submarine and its crew during Sub-Zero), Varies with Preparation, from at least City Block Level (His massive Cold Gun from "Heart of Ice" would have frozen the Gothcorp skyscraper), up to Large Town Level to Large Mountain Level (405 Kilotons to 2.96 Gigatons - Grant Walker's gigantic cold gun would have frozen all of the world's municipalities over several years - this is even further confirmed by the fact that the cannon's core overloading almost instantly froze over the city of Oceania) | At least Small Building Level physically (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - Confirmed to be more powerful than his B:TAS iteration, likely owing to his new suit. Overpowered Batman in a confrontation, ragdolling him with attacks. Shattered a stone wall and embedded his fist in metal with a punch), at least Large Building Level+ with his Cold Gun (9.6 Tons - Should be at least equal to his prior Cold Gun. Flash-froze a dinosaur skeleton), and Town Level to Mountain Level with Preparation (50.65 Kilotons to 370 Megatons - His reverse-fusion bomb would have frozen everything in a ten mile radius (which would be sections of Gotham), scaling it to about 12.5% of this calc) | At least Small Building Level physically (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - His Beyond suit shouldn't be weaker than his TNBA suit, considering it's implied to have been built after said suit), at least Large Building Level+ with his suit's freezing blasts (9.6 Tons - Shouldn't be any weaker than his prior suit's Cold Gun blasts. Created a humongous mass of ice almost instantly. Sent Blight flying, slamming him through what seems to be a stone wall. Pushed away a falling metal scaffolding)

Hypersonic (Scaling to Mach 8.7), possibly Relativistic+ (Scaling to 0.53c) reactions and combat speed (Fought a serious Batman, grabbing him too quickly for him to dodge - Batman can dodge the Cold Gun's laser. Reacted to and braced himself for a kick from an enraged Dick Grayson. Reacted to Batman's thrown Batarang and blasted it with his Cold Gun), Speed of Light attack speed with his Cold Gun (His cold gun is confirmed to be laser-powered, implying the beam from the gun itself is a laser imbued with freezing properties) | Hypersonic (Scaling to Mach 8.7), possibly Relativistic+ (Scaling to 0.53c) reactions and combat speed reactions and combat speed (Tagged a serious Batman with a punch and a grab in their second fight and rushed him during Batman: Vengeance), Speed of Light attack speed with his Cold Gun (We're given no reason to believe this Cold Gun functions differently from the first one) | Hypersonic (Scaling to Mach 8.7), possibly Relativistic+ (Scaling to 0.53c) reactions and combat speed (Shouldn't be any slower than his previous suits, considering it's implied to be the last one he ever built), Speed of Light attack speed with his suit's freezing blasts (His new suit's cold beams are never stated to be laser-powered like his prior cold guns, but we're never given reason to assume they work differently)

At least Small Building Level (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - So durable that Batman cannot hurt him, even in his BTAS suit. Should be capable of withstanding his own attacks due to Newton's third law of motion) | At least Small Building Level (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - Scales to his own AP as per Newton's Third Law. A serious Batman's punch literally bounced off of Mr. Freeze's helmet, not budging him whatsoever, and in Batman: Vengeance, none of Batman's weaponry can do any damage to Freeze's suit) | At least Small Building Level (Upscaling from 0.095 Tons - Shouldn't be any less durable than his TNBA suit, considering it's implied to have been built after said suit)

Without his suit, he cannot survive in above sub-zero temperatures. Note: Bruce Timm has stated that the original DCAU tie-in comics are not canon, with the only tie in comics that have statements to the contrary (other than Batman: The Adventures Continue, which has so many continuity issues that it's essentially impossible to argue it's canon) being Justice League Infinity, the Batman and Harley Quinn tie in comics, and specifically the first annual of Batman Adventures. Ergo, I only consider those three comics canon. Category:Goulden1998 Category:Tier 9
